Splitting rowVerbatim on the pipe delimiter reproduces decision, owner, acceptanceEvidence, status and consequence as exact string equality against the carried cells. sourcePin does not: the rowVerbatim field is '[Security](03-configuration-and-security.md#proposed-permissions-with-honest-outcomes)' while the carried cell is 'Security (03-configuration-and-security.md#proposed-permissions-with-honest-outcomes)'. The observation is that the rule's own compliance test is not uniform across the six fields it governs: five are literal pipe fields and one carries an undocumented markdown-link normalization. A successor that implements the rule as literal substring extraction will produce '[Security](…)' for sourcePin, will see it differ from the inherited cell, and has no statement in the artifact telling it which of the two is the intended derived view.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: I applied the same test the v7 and v8 reviewers applied. It is a legibility gap in a rule authored this generation, which becomes actual only if file 08 moves and a successor mechanizes the re-parse without inspecting the sourcePin transformation.

claimedRepairVerification.result: CONFIRMED against both, with the union of the two requiredRepair texts satisfied rather than the weaker of them. Codex asked for 'an explicit standing successor rule that requires rowVerbatim and all six derived fields to be re-parsed and co-updated whenever the carried row or its live source changes'; the rule fires on 'rowVerbatim, the live file-08 source pin, or any of those six fields', which covers the carried row, its live source, and the derived half. Claude's branch (a) asked to 'restate the guarantee as a standing rule rather than as roster membership'; /parsedCellsDerivedFrom now reads 'Their forward protection is parsedCellCoUpdateRule, not membership in this generation's closed roster', and the rule states 'This rule does not depend on this generation's roster membership.' Codex's fallback branch is also honoured prospectively: the rule obliges the triggering successor to 'include rowVerbatim plus all six fields on that successor's closed roster', which is the enumeration Codex asked for, bound to the generation that actually needs it rather than to this one. The rule adds a REFUSES clause for a status-only refresh that leaves any of the six stale, which neither reviewer required. Residue scan: zero live roster-membership claims for the six cells survive. The only remaining instance is /honestyRepairsFromV3/1, which is frozen historical accounting and is recorded as such.
claimedRepairVerification.refutationAttempted: I tried to break the rule three ways and could not. (1) Self-violation: if v9 itself refreshed rowVerbatim or any of the six, the rule would oblige v9 to roster all seven paths, and it does not roster them. The leaf diff shows rowVerbatim and all six cells byte-unchanged from v8, so the trigger never fires on v9 and there is no self-violation. (2) Vacuousness: the rule's protection could be void if the current parse were already wrong. I re-derived all six from rowVerbatim and five reproduce by exact string equality, with sourcePin a faithful markdown de-rendering — recorded as CLAUDE-V9-ADV-1, not as a defect. (3) Unenforceability: a rule in an artifact that binds NOTHING might confer nothing. It is the same class of self-imposed succession discipline as /basedOn/method's closed roster, which every reviewer in this lineage has enforced and which I enforced here; and removing the rule on a successor would surface as a removed leaf in exactly the diff this protocol runs. The rule is as enforceable as anything in this corpus.
